path: reports-without-source/Jupiter Lend Vaults on Solana Security Audit Report.pdf

findings.title: Typos and Incorrect Comments
findings.description: The codebase contains several code quality issues in the form of typos and misleading comments. These include a comment in context.rs that incorrectly states "No init_if_needed" despite the macro using init_if_needed, a parameter name typo (is_iquidate instead of is_liquidate) in oracle.rs, a variable name typo (remainining_accounts instead of remaining_accounts) in operate.rs and liquidate.rs, a spelling error in comments ("Minium" instead of "Minimum") in constants.rs, and incorrect error code names (CPY instead of CPI) in errors.rs. The root cause is lack of code review and attention to naming consistency. While these do not directly impact functionality, they reduce code clarity and maintainability, potentially leading to confusion during future development or audits. An attacker cannot directly exploit these issues, but they could mislead developers into making incorrect assumptions, especially regarding account initialization behavior. The impact is limited to reduced code quality and potential maintenance errors.

findings.title: Missing init_if_needed for signer supply ATA causes operate() to revert
findings.description: The Operate struct in context.rs requires the signer_supply_token_account to be pre-initialized, but does not use init_if_needed. This means that if a position NFT is transferred or delegated to an account that lacks an associated token account (ATA) for the supply token, the operate() function will revert during account validation. The root cause is the absence of the init_if_needed directive in the account macro. An attacker could exploit this by transferring a position to a fresh wallet without initializing the ATA, thereby blocking legitimate operations such as deposits or withdrawals. While this does not lead to fund loss, it results in a denial-of-service condition for position management, disrupting user interaction with the protocol. The impact is limited to operational disruption without direct financial loss.

findings.title: Absorption reverts when branch with zero id is missing
findings.description: The absorb function reverts if the branch account with id == 0 is not included in the instruction accounts. When the current branch is the base branch, connected_minima_tick is set to i32::MIN, causing the logic to set branch_data.id to 0 and attempt to load the branch with id 0. If this account is not provided, the call fails. The root cause is the assumption that a branch with id 0 must be present during absorption, even though branch IDs typically start at 1. An attacker could trigger a revert by omitting the branch 0 account from the transaction, disrupting the absorption process. This could block liquidation progress, leading to a denial-of-service for critical risk management operations. The impact is limited to operational disruption of liquidations without direct fund loss, hence the low severity classification.
